title: Robust Aggregation for Low-Cost Verifiable Gradient Lottery
useful_signal_summary: At 20% Byzantine and 64 audited coordinates (3.125% coordinate audit cost), lottery-gated trimmed mean improved relative L2 error versus naive mean by 1.46x to 14.60x across four attack modes and reached cosine about 0.894-0.898. However, mean-after-lottery was better after complete dense-attack rejection, and plain trimmed mean was best for sparse spikes, so the combined robust-after-lottery policy is conditionally useful rather than uniformly dominant.

title: Variance-Guided Data Selection for Tiny LM Pretraining
useful_signal_summary: Variance is a useful diagnostic for underrepresented structured data, but it must be constrained by quality and coverage. Raw high variance and high loss both over-selected noisy examples; low variance over-selected common examples; bandpassed variance improved rare-domain loss but traded away common-domain coverage.

useful_signal_summary: The mechanism is verifiable locally, but low-cost random auditing alone did not protect training from strong malicious gradients: 10%, 25%, and 50% audit collapsed accuracy near zero, while 75% audit recovered 0.961 mean accuracy versus 0.966 honest and full-verify baselines.
